title: Ops Bridge Weekly: customer anomaly log and escalation playbook
body:
Summary:

This is the Ops Bridge weekly note capturing the customer-facing anomalies, triage timeline, temporary mitigations, and next-step owners for private (VPC/on-prem) installs from the last run. Intended audience: install sherpas, field SRE, platform-eng on-call, and solutions engineering. This doc intentionally focuses on items that cross multiple silos (networking, node provisioning, runtime).

Attendees (ops bridge channel + meeting 2027-05-12 09:30 PT):
- Maya Chen (install lead)
- Arun Patel (field engineer)
- Samir Rao (platform SRE)
- Lena Ortega (networking)
- Tomás Rivera (customer success escalation)
- Customer network contact: Priya Menon (ACME Corp)

Incident 1 — 2027-05-11 10:03 UTC: transient 502s + long tail latency on inference pool (ACME staging)- Symptoms: 10–20% of requests returned 502/empty-502 with high p95 token latency (~3.2s vs baseline 0.45s).- Customer impact: bursty failures on their canary route during batch processing windows; model generation timeouts for sessions > 512 tokens.- Initial triage: Arun ran quick checks and observed sporadic socket resets on the inference front-proxy (envoy) with many connections in TIME_WAIT and high ephemeral port reuse.

Timeline and findings:
- 10:08 UTC: platform SRE pulled node-level logs; noticed kernel messages about fragmented packets and repeated ICMP 'fragmentation needed' entries on the node that terminates the customer’s routing table.
- 10:12 UTC: Lena ran traceroute and found MTU drop between customer edge and our node (customer edge=1460, host=1500) causing PMTUD failures for some flows.
- 10:25 UTC: Confirmed kube-proxy conntrack table high water (conntrack entries >> expected). Some long-lived TCP half-open from client retries were keeping sockets occupied.
- 10:40 UTC: Temporary mitigation applied — reduced worker concurrency on ingress envoy (max connections per worker from 1024 -> 512) and enabled tcp_mtu_probing on nodes (sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1).

Permanent root cause hypothesis:
- MTU mismatch at the customer edge + aggressive client retry semantics produced fragmented flows; combined with conntrack table pressure and an implicit TCP retransmission loop, this created transient socket resets observed as 502s in the proxy.

Work items and owners:
- ACTION (Lena): coordinate with ACME NOC to align MTU settings and confirm path MTU via iperf/traceroute-bytes — due 2027-05-14 — JIRA NET-3745.
- ACTION (Samir): add conntrack monitoring to the model-pool dashboard (alert when entries > 70% threshold) and automate conntrack gc kick for node scale-down flows — due 2027-05-18 — JIRA DEPLOY-1123.
- ACTION (Arun): bake tcp_mtu_probing into the preflight checklist + node bootstrap script for onprem installs (flag gated) — due 2027-05-17.
- ACTION (Maya): update Ops Bridge runbook with the 5-step mitigation checklist (reduce concurrency, enable MTU probing, escalate to customer NOC, trace ip-paths, open conntrack alert) — due 2027-05-16.

Incident 2 — 2027-05-12 02:14 UTC: slow model warm-start and NFS hang during day-two runbook on prem-customer Omega- Symptoms: model replicas took 6–8 minutes to attach KV cache; pods stuck in ContainerCreating with mount errors referencing stale NFS handles.

Findings:
- The customer's NFS server was returning EINTR on high concurrency reads; kernel logs on node show stale file handle errors followed by re-mounts.
- Kubernetes timed out mount operations; our init-routines treat mount failure as retry-but-proceed, which left pods in limbo for the runtime bootstrap.

Temporary mitigation:
- Field engineer mounted a local emptyDir-backed KV cache to let model runtime boot while NFS team investigates (degraded cold-start performance but service restored).

Follow-ups and owners:
- ACTION (Arun + Customer NOC): escalate NFS firmware and SMB/NFS tuning (rsize/wsize) with customer's infra team. Confirm kernel & nfs-utils versions and recommend patch if below supported baseline — due 2027-05-20.
- ACTION (Samir): make init bootstrap idempotent to fallback to ephemeral disk (emptyDir) if NFS mounts exceed X retries; expose a telemetry flag for these fallbacks — due 2027-05-24.

Operational notes and cross-cutting observations:
- Preflight gaps seen repeatedly: lack of MTU/path tests, inconsistent kernel/NVIDIA driver matrix verification, and missing conntrack sizing for large private pools.
- Observability gaps: current dashboards miss conntrack pressure and PMTU failure signals; we need derived metrics (ICMP fragmentation rates, syslog parsing, and envoy downstream socket resets metric).
- Communication: customers prefer a one-pager preflight summary that maps to our internal checklist (network, MTU, NFS, KMS access, HSM endpoints, firewall rules). Create a templated 'preflight acceptance' doc for every new install.

Proposed changes to deployment playbooks (short list):
1) Add PMTUD verification step (iperf, traceroute -M with payload sizes) to preflight and post-up smoke test.
2) Add conntrack sizing guidance based on expected RPS and connection churn; recommend node-level sysctl defaults.
3) Add a canary startup that warms KV cache on ephemeral disk if NFS mounts fail; log and alert explicitly.
4) Extend runbook to include a standard 'edge-network quick checklist' for partners with brief commands and expected outputs.

Blockers and help requested:
- Customer legal review is delaying acceptance of our KMS/HSM key rotation approach for onprem private installs. This blocks final signoff for two customers (Omega, Nimbus). Requesting security review prioritization from security team. Owner: Tomás (escalation) — QOS needed by 2027-05-20.
- A kernel-driver mismatch has been observed across three on-prem sites (NVIDIA driver 525 vs required 535 for cuFFT improvements), causing occasional OOMs during model warm-up. Platform eng to provide a matrix and a hotfix container image that tolerates older drivers (graceful degradation). Owner: Samir — deliverable 2027-05-25.

Notes for next Ops Bridge meeting (2027-05-19):
- Review progress on MTU confirmations for ACME and other pending customers.
- Validate conntrack alerts and dashboard prototypes (Samir).
- Draft preflight acceptance one-pager and circulate to SEs (Maya).
- Security update on KMS/HSM approvals (Tomás).

Quick links referenced:
- Confluence: Ops-Bridge-Playbook (link in metadata)
- JIRA: DEPLOY-1123 (conntrack + dashboard), NET-3745 (customer MTU), INF-5591 (NFS fallback)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/private-deployments/PR-821 (bootstrap idempotency patch)

Appendix: quick run commands for field engineers (copyable)
- iperf3 client -> server (MTU test): iperf3 -c <customer-edge> -M 1400 -t 10
- traceroute with bytes: traceroute -F -s <src> -m 30 -w 2 <dst>
- conntrack count: sudo conntrack -L | wc -l
- enable tcp_mtu_probing: sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1

If anything needs to be added or corrected, reply in the Ops Bridge doc thread.

-- Maya
